title: Prebuilt Cache Providers and Maturity
readerIntent: Choose a cache provider that matches topology and consistency needs.
summary: NodeCache is process-local reference behavior, Redis is a guarded distributed adapter, and Hazelcast is a fail-closed extension slot until a real adapter is supplied and qualified.

sections.heading: NodeCache
paragraphs: Useful for local development, a single process, or data that tolerates per-process copies. Restart clears it, and it cannot prove cross-node invalidation or strict distributed session semantics.

sections.heading: Redis
paragraphs: The distributed adapter is appropriate for shared channels only after live qualification of connection security, atomic operations, invalidation, failure behavior, capacity, recovery, and supported versions.

sections.heading: Hazelcast
paragraphs: The current slot must fail closed until a project or reusable provider implements the generic adapter contract and passes live cluster tests. Installed local software alone does not activate or qualify it.

sections.heading: Selection
items: Required TTL, atomic consume, prefix flush, serialization, and diagnostics.
Latency, payload size, availability, persistence expectations, and cost.
